title: Affine deformation chart after removing the strict transform
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$ be a finitely generated ideal. Using affine spectra [def-weil-affine-spectrum], set $X=\operatorname{Spec}R[t]$ and $J=(I,t)$. In the blow-up [def-nagata-global-blowup] of $X$ along the closed subscheme $V(J)$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], the scheme-theoretic strict transform [def-nagata-strict-transform] of the closed subscheme $V(t)$ is empty on the $t$-chart $\operatorname{Spec}R[t,I/t]$. On the $f_i$-chart, writing $C=R[I/f_i]$ and $v=t/f_i$, the strict transform is the closed subscheme $V(v)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}C[v]$, and its complement is the overlap with the $t$-chart. Consequently the complement of the strict transform in the blow-up is covered by, and over $\operatorname{Spec}R[t]$ is identified with, the affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}R[t,I/t]$, where $R[t,I/t]\subseteq R[t,t^{-1}]$ is the subalgebra generated by $R[t]$ and the elements $f/t$ for $f\in I$.

source.place: Tags 0804 (lemma-blowing-up-affine), 080D (definition-strict-transform); affine specialization to the centre (I,t), with schematic closure calculated by the kernel on each chart

proof.text: Compare the global blow-up with the affine Rees blow-up on the top affine open. The existing cartesian square for the global affine-chart embedding makes that embedding an isomorphism over an affine base. Transport the ideal along the global-sections isomorphism using affine-blow-up functoriality. The charts for t and the f_i cover, since these elements generate J=(I,t).

source.place: Tags 0804 and 080D; affine chart calculation for the centre (I,t)

proof.text: For a=f_i, define the substitution C[v] to A[J/a] by constants c mapping to c and v mapping to t/a, where C=R[I/a] is the actual subalgebra of R_a. It lands in the chart by induction over polynomial expressions and chart generators. Its image contains every generator of J/a: form the ideal of numerators whose fractions are in that image, using t=a(t/a). Injectivity follows by composing with the expansion A_(C a) to R_a[v] that sends t to av; this composite is the coefficientwise inclusion C[v] into R_a[v]. Thus substitution gives the required ring equivalence, including the zero localization.

source.place: Tags 0804 and 080D; affine chart calculation for the centre (I,t)

proof.text: Use the proved strict-transform/blow-up kernel theorem (Tag 080E), in its existing chart-model kernel form: the strict-transform ideal equals the kernel of the map from the blow-up of the pulled-back ideal. Apply the affine/global comparison on both sides. Restrict that affine-blow-up map to a chart using its cartesian chart square and flat base change of kernels along the open chart. The resulting map is strictChartMap composed with the tensor-product right inclusion. Its value in the ambient localization is the ordinary localization map on the chart subalgebra.

source.place: Tag 080E (strict transform as the blow-up of the pulled-back ideal), using the existing kernel and chart-pullback theorems

proof.text: For the hyperplane quotient B=A/(t), the image of t is zero. Its parameter-chart localization is therefore the zero ring, and its chart subalgebra has empty spectrum. The chart kernel from the preceding step is consequently the unit ideal.

source.place: Tags 0804 and 080D; affine chart calculation for the centre (I,t)

proof.text: On the a-chart, compose the chart map to B_(a) with the polynomial substitution. It sends v to zero and maps each coefficient by the localization of the injective constants map R to A/(t). This localized constants map is injective, so a polynomial is in its kernel exactly when its constant coefficient is zero, equivalently when it belongs to (v). Closed-immersion and ring-equivalence kernel transport then identify the strict-transform ideal on the stated polynomial chart with the kernel of the quotient by (v).

source.place: Tags 0804 and 080D; affine chart calculation for the centre (I,t)

proof.text: The standard-open preimage formula for Proj identifies the inverse image of the t-chart on the a-chart with the basic open of the homogeneous ratio (tz)/(az). The explicit homogeneous-away chart map sends this ratio to t/a. Under the polynomial equivalence this is v, so the overlap is exactly D(v). The support of the quotient kernel (v) is V(v), hence its complement is that overlap.

source.place: Tags 0804 and 080D; affine chart calculation for the centre (I,t)

proof.text: The parameter chart lies outside the strict-transform support, and the finite chart cover and the preceding overlap calculation put every point outside that support in the parameter chart. Equality of these open sets, together with the open immersion of the chart, gives the required isomorphism to the complement; the chart-to-base formula verifies that it is over Spec A. Finally, the subalgebra generated by J/t equals that generated by all constants f/t: use the ideal of numerators whose fractions lie in the latter subalgebra, noting t/t=1.
